content:
### Recommendation: **Strategy 2, with Strategy 1 as the fallback when headroom matters.**

Dual-resident serialized inference is the right default because:

1. It preserves **100 % of each model's solo throughput** — concurrency destroyed half of it.
2. The switch cost it avoids (~7 s) is comparable to a single 9B response, so avoiding reloads is
   worth real money on an agent loop that alternates workers.
3. Co-residency was stable: 100 % success over 344 steps, no leak, desktop intact.

**But it is a deliberate trade, and the escape hatch matters.** Free VRAM falls to ~1.0 GB,
below the ≥2 GB the specification asks for. If the desktop load grows (browser, IDE, video
call), WDDM may start spilling to shared system memory — which degrades latency *silently*
rather than failing. So:

- default to **Strategy 2** for agent workloads;
- fall back to **Strategy 1** when doing VRAM-heavy work, or when `nvidia-smi` shows free VRAM
  approaching 1 GB;
- **never** adopt Strategy 3.

This overturns the original specification's assumption that `local-smart` must be
**EXCLUSIVE**. It does not need to be: it can be **RESIDENT alongside `local-fast`**, with
inference serialised.

## 6. Co-residency — the Phase 3 core experiment

Both models loaded simultaneously (`local-fast` :8111 with 8K, `local-smart` :8112 with 16K).

| Measure | 4B alone | 9B alone | **Both resident** |
|---|---|---|---|
| GPU `self` (llama.cpp attribution) | 2981 MiB | 5527 MiB | **8508 MiB** |
| GPU total used (incl. desktop) | 5183 MiB | 7724 MiB | **10,848–10,923 MiB** |
| **Free VRAM** | 6762 MiB | 4221 MiB | **~1030–1090 MiB** |
| Desktop GUI stable | — | — | **yes** (explorer + dwm alive) |
| Shared-memory spill | — | — | **none observed** |
| CUDA OOM | — | — | **none** |
| 100 % success over 344 stability steps | — | — | **yes** |

**Co-residency is possible.** Both models fit, the desktop stayed responsive, and a 6-minute
stability run with both loaded completed at 100 %.

**But the free VRAM is ~1.0 GB, below the ≥2 GB the specification asks for.** That is the
honest cost. It worked in this test with the current desktop load; a heavier desktop
(browser + IDE + video) could push it into the WDDM shared-memory path, which would silently
destroy latency rather than fail loudly.

### Strategy 2 — dual resident, serialized inference
- Both models always hot; peak VRAM ~10.9 GB, **~1.0 GB free**
- Every request gets its full solo throughput (123.5 / 73.6 t/s)
- A single global GPU semaphore adds queueing latency but no throughput loss
- **Best for: interactive agent use where switch latency matters more than headroom.**

# =============================================================================
# coresidency.ps1 - Phase 3 core experiment
#
# Answers: should local-fast and local-smart be RESIDENT together on a 12 GB card,
# or does local-smart need EXCLUSIVE residency? Measures the three strategies:
#
#   Strategy 1  unload/reload        (one model resident at a time)
#   Strategy 2  dual resident, serialized inference
#   Strategy 3  dual resident, concurrent inference
#
# Usage:
#   powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\coresidency.ps1 -Mode alone9b
#   powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\coresidency.ps1 -Mode both
#   powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\coresidency.ps1 -Mode reload
# =============================================================================

param(
  [ValidateSet('alone4b','alone9b','both','reload','concurrent')][string]$Mode = 'alone9b',
  [string]$Quant9B = 'Q4_K_M',
  [int]$Ctx9B = 8192,
  [int]$Ctx4B = 8192,
  [int]$Reps = 3
)

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'
$Llama   = 'D:\MultiAgent\tools\llama.cpp\b11254-cuda13.4'
$Bench   = Join-Path $Llama 'llama-bench.exe'
$Server  = Join-Path $Llama 'llama-server.exe'
$Models  = 'D:\MultiAgent\models\llm'
$Results = 'D:\MultiAgent\benchmarks\local-smart\results'
$Logs    = 'D:\MultiAgent\logs'
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $Results | Out-Null

$m4b = Join-Path $Models 'Qwen3.5-4B-Q4_K_M.gguf'
$m9b = Join-Path $Models "Qwen3.5-9B-$Quant9B.gguf"

function Vram([string]$which) {
  return [int]((& nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.$which --format=csv,noheader,nounits) -replace '\s','')
}
function PsLine { param([string]$tag) [pscustomobject]@{ tag=$tag; used=Vram 'used'; free=Vram 'free' } }

function BenchOne {
  param([string]$Model, [string]$Tag, [int]$Ctx = 0, [int]$Secs = 60)
  $args = @('-m', $Model, '-ngl', '99', '-t', '12', '-p', '512', '-n', '128', '-r', $Reps, '-o', 'csv')
  $of = Join-Path $Logs "co_$Tag.out"; $ef = Join-Path $Logs "co_$Tag.err"
  $vw = Join-Path $Results "vram_co_$Tag.csv"
  $p = Start-Process -FilePath $Bench -ArgumentList $args -PassThru -WindowStyle Hidden `
         -RedirectStandardOutput $of -RedirectStandardError $ef
  & 'D:\MultiAgent\scripts\vram_watch.ps1' -Seconds $Secs -IntervalMs 400 -OutFile $vw | Out-Null
  $p.WaitForExit(900000) | Out-Null
  if (-not $p.HasExited) { $p.Kill() }

  $rows = Get-Content $of -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_.StartsWith('"') }
  $pp = $null; $tg = $null
  foreach ($r in $rows) {
    $f = $r -split ','
    $np = ($f[34] -replace '"','').Trim()
    $ts = [double](($f[40] -replace '"','').Trim())
    if ($np -ne '0') { $pp = $ts } else { $tg = $ts }
  }
  $peak = $null; $util = $null; $pwr = $null
  if (Test-Path $vw) {
    $d = Import-Csv $vw
    if ($d) {
      $peak = ($d | Measure-Object mem_used_mb -Maximum).Maximum
      $util = [math]::Round(($d | Measure-Object gpu_util -Average).Average,1)
      $pwr  = ($d | Measure-Object power_w -Maximum).Maximum
    }
  }
  return [pscustomobject]@{ tag=$Tag; prompt_tps=$pp; gen_tps=$tg; peak_vram=$peak; util=$util; power=$pwr }
}

function StartServer {
  param([string]$Model, [string]$Alias, [int]$Port, [int]$Ctx, [string]$Tag)
  $args = @('-m',$Model,'--alias',$Alias,'-ngl','99','-c',$Ctx,'-np','1','-t','12',
            '-b','2048','-ub','512','--flash-attn','auto','-ctk','f16','-ctv','f16',
            '--host','127.0.0.1','--port',$Port,'--cors-origins','localhost',
            '--no-cors-credentials','--no-webui','--log-jsonl',
            '--log-file',(Join-Path $Logs "$Tag.server.jsonl"))
  $p = Start-Process -FilePath $Server -ArgumentList $args -PassThru -WindowStyle Hidden `
         -RedirectStandardOutput (Join-Path $Logs "$Tag.out") -RedirectStandardError (Join-Path $Logs "$Tag.err")
  for ($i=0; $i -lt 180; $i++) {
    Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 1000
    try { $h = Invoke-RestMethod "http://127.0.0.1:$Port/health" -TimeoutSec 3
          if ($h.status -eq 'ok') { return $p } } catch {}
    if ($p.HasExited) { return $null }
  }
  return $null
}

function StopAny {
  Get-Process -Name llama-server -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Stop-Process -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
  Start-Sleep -Seconds 3
}

- **Throughput collapses ~47 %.** Two parallel requests complete slower in aggregate than
  sequential ones.
- No compensating benefit.
- **Not recommended.**
